--- title: "Philadelphia Housing Price Prediction" subtitle: "A Predictive Modeling Framework to Support Property Tax Assessment" author: "Daisy, Liz, Johnny, Parker" date: "March 17, 2026" format: revealjs: theme: simple slide-number: true slide-level: 2 chalkboard: true code-line-numbers: true incremental: false smaller: true scrollable: true --- ::: {.cell} ::: # Research Question & Motivation {visibility="hidden"} ## Research Question & Motivation :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Research Question - Background: Philadelphia is seeking to improve its **Automated Valuation Model**. - Research question: How can residential sale prices prediction be **more accurate** spagial and demographic? - Analytical scope: The segment of residential **marketing** sales. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Motivation - Property tax assessment depends on **credible estimates** of market value. - Inaccurate valuation can lead to **unequal policy** - Better prediction help **strengthen AVM** ::: :::: --- # Data Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## Data Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} 🏠 ### Property Data - Residential sales records - Sale price - Interior area - Bedrooms / bathrooms - Year built - Property type ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} 🏘️ ### Neighborhood Data - ACS census variables - Median income - Poverty - Education - Demographic structure ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} 📍 ### Spatial Data - Transit access - Park proximity - Distance-based accessibility - Other city or amenity measures ::: :::: *Together, these sources capture property characteristics, neighborhood market conditions, and their location information.* --- ## Data Source & Cleaning **Source:** OPA Properties Public Dataset — 2023–2024 Residential Sales, Philadelphia
:::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} **🗂 Filter 1: Basic Info** - Residential: Single Family & Multi Family - Years: sales in 2023 & 2024 - State: PA only ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} **🚫 Filter 2: Implausible Values** - Living area: > 0 sq ft - Bedrooms: > 0 - **Sale price: > $50,000** ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} **❓ Filter 3: Missing Values** - Sale price - Living area - Bedrooms & bathrooms - All model variables ::: :::: --- *23372 residential sales across Philadelphia, 2023–2024.* # Key Visualizations {visibility="hidden"} ## Spatial Distribution of Residential Sale Prices ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: --- ## Properties Sold by Census Tract ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: --- ## Spatial Autocorrelation of Sale Prices ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: **Key takeaways:**

**High-High** clusters concentrate in **Center City and Chestnut Hill**, with smaller clusters in Far Northeast, around UPenn, and the far southern tip.
**Low-Low** clusters dominate **North and West Philadelphia**.
The absence of significant autocorrelation at the boundary suggests an abrupt spatial discontinuity. --- # Model Comparison {visibility="hidden"} ## Model Performance Improves with Each Layer ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
10-Fold Cross-Validation Results
Model RMSE (log) Approx. Error (%) MAE (log) R²
M7: + Neighborhood FE 0.4224 52.6 0.2734 0.6212
M5b: + Spatial 0.4436 55.8 0.2974 0.5824
M4: + Census 0.4561 57.8 0.3088 0.5584
M3: Structural Only 0.5369 71.1 0.3948 0.3883
````` ::: ::: **Bottom line:** Model performance improves at each stage, with the largest gain from adding **neighborhood context**. The final model with neighborhood fixed effects performs best, though prediction error remains meaningful. --- # Main Findings {visibility="hidden"} ## Most Influential Predictors ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: **Key Takeaways:** - Size dominates: Living area is the strongest single predictor - Socioeconomics outweigh amenities: BA+ education share and poverty rate have larger effects than transit access or school proximity, confirming that *who lives nearby* matters more than *what's nearby*. - Bathrooms signal overall quality: Unlike bedrooms, bathrooms carry a strong premium because they proxy for renovation level and overall property condition. ## Final Model Data Errors ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} M7 predicts mid-range prices well, but systematically **overestimates low-price properties** and struggles with **luxury outliers** — consistent with limited training data at the extremes. ::: --- ## Final Model Spatial Errors ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Daisy_Yuan_Presentation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: **Bottom line:** The residuals from M7 are relatively dispersed rather than forming large, continuous clusters, which suggests that the final model captures much of the broad spatial structure in Philadelphia’s housing market. At the same time, small pockets of over- and under-prediction remain across the city, indicating that some localized market variation is still not fully explained. --- # Policy Recommendations {visibility="hidden"} ## Risks and Limitations for OPA :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Risks - Neighborhood fixed effects may encode historical racial or economic bias - Excluding low-end outliers removes properties in lower-income communities from the model — residents in these areas may not benefit from accurate AVM assessments or fair tax policy protections - Missing data exclusions may further reduce representation of disadvantaged neighborhoods ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Limitations - A single citywide model relies on historical prices and cannot capture rapid local shifts — such as price jumps in gentrifying areas - Trained on 2023–2024 only — unable to reflect longer market cycles ::: :::: --- ## Recommendations for Strengthening the AVM - **Add more variables**: Incorporate building permits and recent renovation records to capture localized market dynamics - **Build sub-models by area**: Develop neighborhood-specific models for rapidly changing markets rather than applying a single citywide specification - **Update regularly**: Retrain the model annually with new sales data to prevent predictions from lagging behind market conditions - **Flag outliers for manual review**: Properties with unusually large residuals should be flagged and reviewed before entering formal tax assessment - **Reconsider low-price sample exclusions**: Design a targeted strategy for low-value properties to ensure lower-income communities are not systematically excluded from AVM protections

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
